Mohammad Abdullah Bhat And Another vs Mohammad Akram
Teli And Another on 16 April, 2024
Author: Javed Iqbal Wani

Bench: Javed Iqbal Wani
 S. No. 15
In The High Court Of Jammu & Kashmir And Ladakh
 At Srinagar

entities.text:
High Court Of Jammu & Kashmir And Ladakh
 At Srinagar
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Mohammad Abdullah Bhat and Another ...Petitioner(s)

Through: Mr. Z. A. Qureshi, Sr. Advocate with
 Mr. Agha Faisal Ali, Advocate.

Vs.
Mohammad Akram Teli and Another ...Respondent(s)
Through: Mr. Aatir Javid Kawoosa, Advocate.
 Ms. Suwaiba, Advocate.

Coram:
 Hon'Ble Mr Justice Javed Iqbal Wani, Judge
 Order

1. In the instant appeal filed under Section 173 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, (for short the Act of 1988) the appellants herein have questioned the award dated 04.04.2014 passed by the Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal Baramulla (for short the Tribunal) in claim petition titled as "Mohammad Akram Telli Vs. Khurshid Ahmad Bhat and Ors."
2. Facts giving rise to the filing of instant appeal are that a claim petition came to be filed by respondent 1 under the provisions of the Act of 1988 before the Tribunal for compensation for the death of his minor daughter namely Zubaida of age 7 years having died in a vehicular accident caused by vehicle/tractor bearing registration No. JK01B- 8337 (for short the offending vehicle)
driven rashly and negligently by its driver being appellant 2 herein owned by appellant 1 herein.

entities.text: Mohammad Akram Telli Vs. Khurshid Ahmad Bhat and Ors
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 3. The Tribunal after having entertained the claim petition summoned the respondents in the claim petition being appellants herein as also the Insurance Company being respondent No. 2 herein with which the offending tractor was stated to be insured.

The aforesaid respondents in the claim petition appeared before the Tribunal and filed their respective objections to the claim petition and though initially the appellants herein were only impleaded as party respondents in the claim petition the Insurance Company respondent 2 herein came to impleaded as party respondent in the claim petition subsequently.

4. On the pleadings of the parties, the Tribunal framed the following issues: -

1 1.

sentences.text: Whether the respondent No.1 on 23.09.1996 was driving offending vehicle rashly and negligently and hit the deceased resulting in multiple injuries and caused his death ?
OPP 2.
If the Issue No.1 is proved in affirmative to what amount of compensation the petitioner is entitled to ?
OPP 3.
Whether the vehicle was insured with respondent No.3, as such the owner is not liable for compensation ?
OPR-2 4.
Whether the respondent driver was not holding a valid driving license at the relevant time and as such the insurance company cannot be saddled with liability?

The claimant respondent 1 herein appeared as his own witness besides examining three more witnesses to prove issues 1 and 2 onus whereof to prove was put on him,
whereas the respondents 1 and 2 in the claim petition being the present appellants did not lead any evidence, however the insurance company respondent 2 herein produced two witnesses namely Mohammad Sultan Shagoo and Mohd Nayeem Khan.

6. The Tribunal after adjudicating upon the claim petition and considering the material on record including the aforesaid evidence lead by the parties held the claimant respondent 1 herein entitled to compensation and consequently in terms of the impugned award granted Rs.3,70,000/- as compensation along with simple interest @ 7% p.a. from the date of institution of claim petition till the final realization of the award amount.

The Tribunal, however, in terms of the impugned award directed the amount of compensation to be paid by the Insurance Company respondent No. 2 herein to the claimant respondent 1 herein and thereafter to be recovered by the insurance company from the respondents 1 and 2 appellants herein.

7. The impugned award is being challenged by the appellants on multiple grounds including on the ground that the Tribunal wrongly provided a right of recovery to the Insurance Company respondent 2 herein of the award amount from the appellants being against the facts and law and that on the date of accident i.e. 23.09.1996 the appellant driver was holding a valid learners driving license which fact was not taken into consideration by the Tribunal and that the Tribunal as well passed the impugned award on a higher side overlooking the law laid down by the Apex Court in a case reported in 2003(7) SCC 484 and 2006(13)SCC 60.
Heard appearing counsel for the parties and perused the record.

8. It is an admitted fact that insofar as the issues 1 and 2 framed by the Tribunal are concerned, onus to prove the said issues was put on the claimant and record tends to show that the claimant besides appearing as his own witness in witness box have had examined witnesses namely Gh. Mohammad Mohammad Abdullah Bhat And Another vs Mohammad Akram Teli And Another on 16 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/67761188/
2 Telli S/o Ab. Karim Telli, Mst. Mukhty widow of Gh. Nabi and Riyaz Ahmad Telli S/o Ab. Razak Telli as his witnesses.

A bare perusal of the statements of the said witnesses demonstrate that claimant has by clinching evidence proved the fact that the accident came to be caused by the offending vehicle on 23.09.1996 causing injuries to the deceased which injuries resulted into her death, as also the amount of compensation, the claimant, as such, became entitled thereto.

Record also shows that during cross examination of said witnesses by the counsel for the respondents appellants herein, the statements of the said witnesses has not been either got discredited or contradicted.

9. Further perusal of the record of the Tribunal reveals that insofar as issue no. 3 is concerned, the onus to prove the same had been put on respondent 2 the owner of the vehicle being appellant 1 herein who indisputably did not lead any evidence in this regard though had not to prove that the vehicle was insured with the Insurance Company yet, failed to prove that he is not liable to pay compensation to the claimant.

10. Record of the tribunal further reveals that insofar as the issue 4 supra is concerned , indisputably the onus to prove the said issue had been put on the Insurance Company respondent herein and to discharge the said onus, as has been noticed in the preceding paras, the Insurance Company examined above named two witnesses to prove that the driver of the offending vehicle was not holding a valid driving license at the time of accident thus, not rendering the Insurance company being liable to pay compensation to the claimant.

Perusal of the statements of the witnesses produced by the Insurance Company respondent 2 herein tends to show that the witness namely Mohammad Sultan Shagoo Sr. Assistant, RTO Office Srinagar have had deposed during examination in chief before the Tribunal that the learners license of the driver of offending vehicle bearing No. 7653 dated 03.08.1996 pursuant to the record stands issued in the name of one Mohammad Shafi S/o Gh Mohammad R/o Aali Kadal Srinagar and has not been issued in the name of driver of the vehicle namely Khurshid Ahmad Bhat and had further stated during cross examination that the said license No. 7653 in terms of the record stands issued on 03.11.2001.
The said witness during his cross examination has further deposed that he cannot say which RTO has issued the learners license to the driver of the offending vehicle as he does not remember his name.

The witnesses namely Mohammad Nayeem Khan in his statement before the Tribunal has stated that he came to be appointed by Insurance company to conduct verification of the driving license of the driver of the offending vehicle and in this regard he addressed a communication to the office of RTO Srinagar in response to which the office of RTO vide letter dated 13.08.2011 stated that the learners license remains valid for six months and same gets expired after the said date.
The said witness also produced the said letter of the office of RTO and same had been taken on record.

During the cross examination, the said witness stated that in the photocopy of the license in question he is not in a position to clarify number and other particulars as the same can be explained by the RTO.

11. Having regard to the aforesaid evidence produced before the Tribunal qua issue no. 4, the Insurance Company respondent 2 herein indisputably has proved the fact that the driver of the Mohammad Abdullah Bhat And Another vs Mohammad Akram Teli And Another on 16 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/67761188/
3 offending vehicle was not holding a valid license at the time of accident

entities.text: Mohammad Abdullah Bhat And Another vs Mohammad Akram Teli And Another
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: and as has been noticed in the preceding paras, on the contrary neither the owner of the tractor nor the driver of the tractor being the appellants herein have either led any evidence to show that the driver of the offending vehicle was holding an effective driving license on the date of accident nor did contradict and dispute the evidence in this regard led by the Insurance Company respondent 2 herein.
The Insurance Company the respondent 2 thus can safely be said to have discharged the onus to prove issue no. 4 before the Tribunal.

12. Insofar as the ground urged by the appellants qua the quantum of compensation is concerned,
the said ground cannot be accepted in view of the position of law laid down by the Apex court and rightly relied upon by the Tribunal in case titled as "Kishan Gopal and Anr. Vs. Lala and Ors"
reported in 2014(1) SCC 244.

entities.text: Kishan Gopal and Anr. Vs. Lala and Ors
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
The Tribunal cannot be, but, said to have passed a fair and just compensation in the matter in favour of the claimant respondent 1 herein and rightly in terms of the impugned award directed the owner and driver of offending vehicle being appellants herein to pay compensation to the claimant respondent 1 herein to be paid in the first instance by the Insurance Company respondent 2 herein, granting right of recovery to the Insurance Company respondent 2 to recover the said amount of compensation from the appellants.
13.
The Tribunal in view of above cannot be said to have committed any fault, illegality or perversity while passing the impugned award.
14. For the aforesaid reasons, the impugned award does not call for interference.
Resultantly the appeal fails and is accordingly dismissed.

15. Registry to remit back the record to the Tribunal.
Dismissed.
(JAVED IQBAL WANI) JUDGE SRINAGAR 16.04.2024
